sections.html:
Toombs County is in southeast Georgia, with Lyons holding the courthouse and Vidalia ranking as the biggest city. The cities are Lyons, Santa Claus and Vidalia, and Center, English Eddy, Normantown and South Thompson have no municipal government. The Toombs County School District runs the public schools.

Houses here are the least expensive of the Georgia counties near it. The 2020-2024 median is $137,000, and owners occupy 60.5% of units. The county recorded just 35 building permits for 2025, so nearly every sale involves an existing house. Of 12,027 housing units counted in 2020, 12.7% were empty. Population is estimated at 27,545 for mid-2025, up 1.9% from the 2020 base.

sections.h2: Which office mails the bill and which sets the value
sections.html:
The commissioner handles billing and collection from 100 Courthouse Square, Suite 169, Lyons, GA 30436. The phone is (912) 526-8575. Weekday service runs from half past eight to half past four.

The assessors, who determine value and take returns and exemption forms, answer at (912) 526-6291. For a copy of your warranty deed, go to the clerk of superior court's deed room in the courthouse.

  • Tax commissioner: statements, payments, decals for mobile homes, delinquent sales
  • Assessors: valuation, returns, homestead filings, first-level appeals
  • Equalization board: named by the Grand Jury to hear disputes
  • County commissioners and school board: adopt the millage rates

The commissioner does not decide value or rates. Anyone upset about how large the bill is should talk to the elected boards that levy it.

Statements leave the office by October 20. Real estate and business personal property bills have been due November 15 since 2018, while Georgia's default is December 20. Rely on the date on your own statement and call (912) 526-8575 if it looks off.

After the deadline, interest runs at 1% monthly and a 10% penalty applies to tax unpaid 90 days out. Past 30 days, a fi. fa., which is a recorded lien, may be filed. Those records are open to the public, so credit bureaus can see them.

  • Interest on real estate: 1% each month
  • Penalty once 90 days pass: 10%
  • Lien: allowed once 30 days pass unpaid
  • Mobile homes: April 1, then 10% plus 1% a month

Delinquent parcels can go to an auction on the courthouse steps. The list for any sale can be seen at the office, where staff can tell you the next one.

Before you sign a contract, have the commissioner state the parcel's balance in writing. Georgia gives no refund for a part year, which leaves the January 1 owner holding the whole amount.

Lyons, Santa Claus and Vidalia are cities, and a home inside one may owe city tax along with county tax. Ask whether both apply. If you have fallen behind, check the clerk's records for a recorded lien too, since a title company will want it released. When the roof, wiring or plumbing needs money you lack, an as-is cash buyer removes the repair bill, and any tax owed comes out of the price at closing.

A clear payoff letter and a copy of the recorded deed are the two papers that move a closing fastest. Ask the office how long each figure stays valid, since interest adds every month and an old quote will come up short.

Toombs County sellers can head off most tax delays with a few calls.

  1. Ask the commissioner for a written balance on every open year and any mobile home account.
  2. If the house is inside Lyons, Santa Claus or Vidalia, ask the city about its own bill.
  3. Ask the assessors whether your homestead exemption is on file, since the buyer will start from a clean slate.
  4. Get a copy of your recorded deed from the clerk's deed room.
  5. Hand all of it to the closing agent, who will pay the balances out of your proceeds.

Homes that were rentals or came through an estate tend to carry older balances, so start there. A cash buyer can close on a house with open tax and sort out the payoff at the table.

Anything taxable that you own on January 1 is supposed to be returned to the assessors during the first three months of the year, ending April 1. An owner who files nothing is treated as repeating last year's final value and real estate exemptions.

An owner who thinks the value is too high may file a return giving their own opinion of market value, and that filing establishes appeal rights if the assessors change the figure again. The commissioner bills real property, personal property, motor vehicle, mobile home and timber taxes.

  • Window: opens January 1, closes April 1
  • Silence: last year's value and exemptions repeat
  • Own-value return: sets up an appeal if the assessors disagree

Household goods are not normally taxable, so a seller does not owe tax on furniture left in the house.

The regular exemption goes to owners who live in the house before January 1. The amounts are $20,000 off assessed value for county operations, $2,000 off county school tax and $2,000 off the state share. A city house gets a further $10,000 off city and city school tax.

Further categories carry labels: S3 for age 62 and up with an income test, S4 and SC for age 65 and up, SS for unremarried surviving spouses, and a local school-tax exemption at 70 and over. The 62-and-over school exemption uses a $10,000 earned-income limit for the prior year. Because details vary by category, ask the assessors which one fits your situation.

Applications are received between January 1 and April 1, and state law allows no extension. Once approved, the exemption repeats yearly until eligibility changes. Moving to a new address means filing again.

Mail a letter to the Toombs County assessors. The 45 days are counted from the date on the notice, and notices tend to arrive in spring.

Valid grounds are taxability, value, uniformity or a refused exemption. Three tracks are open: the equalization board, a hearing officer, or arbitration. A dispute can then move on to Superior Court. Mobile homes keep a separate clock. A different value may be declared inside 45 days of the bill mailing, and a change notice opens a 21-day window to go to the equalization board.

faqs.q: What is the best way to reach the Toombs County tax commissioner?
faqs.a: Phone (912) 526-8575 or visit 100 Courthouse Square, Suite 169, in Lyons, any weekday between half past eight and half past four.

faqs.q: Does Toombs County tax come due in November or December?
faqs.a: Real estate bills have been due November 15 since 2018, and December 20 is the state default. Use the date on your bill, and double-check with the commissioner.

faqs.q: What does paying Toombs County tax late cost?
faqs.a: One percent interest accrues monthly after the deadline, and tax still open 90 days later takes a 10% penalty. A lien may be filed after 30 days.

faqs.q: When are Toombs County mobile home taxes due?
faqs.a: They fall due each April 1. Later payments draw a 10% filing penalty plus 1% per month, and a location permit and decal come only after full payment.

faqs.q: How much time does an owner get to dispute a Toombs County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days, starting at the date on the assessment notice. Write to the assessors and say which route you want: equalization board, hearing officer or arbitrator.
